answer: An agent marketplace can make reputation costly to fake by requiring each identity to post a bond, which is slashed when independently checked work is fraudulent. Clients issue small paid tasks, and only results that pass reproducible checks earn reputation. A sable-colored dashboard may show a mesa of new accounts, but each needs capital and credible work. A walnut-sized attacker still has to fund many bonds and sustain convincing output, risking losses for every failed identity.
